title: CHAPTER 6: FLORA, FAUNA AND PROTECTED AREAS

blocks.content: Arunachal Pradesh is a biodiversity hotspot of global significance. It forms part of the Indo-Burma biodiversity hotspot and the Eastern Himalaya biodiversity hotspot. With over 80% of its area under forest cover, it harbours an astonishing variety of plant and animal life.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Namdapha National Park is renowned for harboring four big cat species: Tiger, Leopard, Clouded Leopard, and Snow Leopard.
Eaglenest Wildlife Sanctuary is globally celebrated as a premier birding paradise in the Eastern Himalayas.
The region displays a diverse altitudinal range featuring tropical evergreen, sub-tropical, temperate, and alpine vegetation.
Protected areas in this region harbor rare, endemic, and threatened species of flora and fauna.

cells: Below 500 m; Changlang, Tirap, Lohit, Namsai foothills

blocks.content: Arunachal Pradesh has one of the richest plant diversities in Asia. It is estimated to have over 5,000 species of flowering plants, 500+ species of orchids, and hundreds of medicinal plant species.

items: Orchids: Over 500–600 species including Rhynchostylis retusa (State Flower), Vanda coerulea (Blue Vanda — endangered)
Rhododendrons: Over 100 species; state flower of neighbouring Sikkim; mass blooms in spring
Medicinal plants: Taxus wallichiana (Himalayan Yew — source of taxol), Rauvolfia serpentina, Podophyllum hexandrum
Bamboo: Over 100 species; crucial for tribal livelihood and construction
Ferns: Over 500 species, including tree ferns in warmer zones
The state tree is Hollong (Dipterocarpus macrocarpus) — a tropical evergreen timber tree
State flower: Foxtail Orchid (Rhynchostylis retusa) — known locally as Kopou Phool

blocks.content: The Takin (Budorcas taxicolor) is the State Animal of Arunachal Pradesh. It is a massive bovid found in the bamboo forests of the Eastern Himalayas, including Tawang and West Kameng districts.

The Great Hornbill (Buceros bicornis) is the State Bird. It holds great cultural significance for many tribes; the Nyishi traditionally used its beak in their Bopia headgear, which has now been replaced by fibreglass replicas to protect the species.

Hundreds of orchid species; unique in India

items: Namdapha National Park is frequently asked in UPSC/State PSC exams for being the only national park in India hosting four species of big cats.
Eaglenest Wildlife Sanctuary is famous for the discovery of the critically endangered bird species, Bugun Liocichla.
Note the geographical locations: Namdapha is in the Changlang district while Eaglenest is in the West Kameng district of Arunachal Pradesh.

blocks.content: Namdapha is one of India's most biodiverse national parks and is the third largest in the country. It is the only park in the world where all four felid species of big cats — tiger, leopard, clouded leopard, and snow leopard — coexist. It is also a part of the Indo-Burma biodiversity hotspot and has exceptional bird diversity with over 400 species recorded.
Eagle Nest Wildlife Sanctuary — Birding Paradise

Eagle Nest WLS in West Kameng district is widely regarded as one of the best bird-watching sites in the world. It is famous for the discovery of the Bugun Liocichla (Liocichla bugunorum), a new bird species discovered as late as 2006. The sanctuary hosts over 450 bird species and attracts birdwatchers from across the globe.
